symbol_descriptions: Initial product formation rate in micromoles per liter per second

new_symbol_range_suggestions.K_H_app: positive; choose comparable to the swept H range and not necessarily equal to K_H, so denominator H-sensitivity can be distinguished from catalytic-competence modulation

derivation_notes: The parent used one shared environmental midpoint for both catalytic competence and apparent binding/inhibition effects. Here the denominator keeps the same finite-capacity occupancy form but its H-dependence is allowed to saturate around a distinct midpoint K_H_app, representing protonation-linked binding or inhibitory microstates that need not align with the catalytic transition.
change_summary: Relaxed the shared-threshold assumption by giving the denominator H-response its own environmental half-effect input K_H_app while preserving the original catalytic-competence Hill factor. This creates substrate-dependent curvature in v0 versus H because low-S assays are dominated by numerator competence modulation whereas higher-S assays also feel the shifted denominator transition.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: One shared Hill-like environmental transition is sufficient for both catalytic competence and apparent affinity/substrate-inhibition behavior.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Different protonation-linked microstates can control chemistry at the catalytic step and substrate/inhibitor binding energetics with distinct environmental sensitivities, so the H-dependence of turnover need not align with the H-dependence of apparent binding/inhibition.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when K_H_app = K_H, so the denominator and catalytic-competence terms share the same environmental midpoint again.

response_change.parent_relation: The current mapping makes the environmental effect enter through one shared half-effect scale K_H, so at fixed substrate the H-dependence is a single Hill-like transition that uniformly rescales the Michaelis-Menten-with-substrate-inhibition rate.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that the same environmental midpoint governs both catalytic competence and affinity/inhibition effects; allow the environment dependence already present in the denominator to have a distinct H-sensitivity from the numerator competence term, creating substrate-dependent bending of v0 versus H.
response_change.observable_effect: At low versus intermediate/high substrate, the H value where rate changes most strongly can shift, so normalized v0(H) curves no longer collapse to one common transition after simple rescaling.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when H is swept across the transition region and substrate is varied from low occupancy (S comparable to or below K_M) into regimes where saturation or substrate inhibition matters (S comparable to K_M and/or sqrt(K_M*K_I) to above), so denominator and numerator H-effects are both consequential.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, low-S assays mainly report catalytic-competence modulation, while higher-S assays expose the H-dependent affinity/inhibition curvature; in holdout, broader H sweeps or more strongly inhibitory S make the shifted H-response more pronounced.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by forcing the environmental midpoint/steepness governing affinity and inhibition changes to coincide with the catalytic-competence midpoint/steepness, or by making the extra distinction vanish so all H-dependence shares the same K_H transition.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: Existing symbols provide only one environmental scale K_H for all H effects. A distinct independently sampled condition is unnecessary, but one additional environmental-response input is needed if the benchmark requires separating the H sensitivity of binding/inhibition from that of catalytic competence without conflating them into the same shared transition.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: distinct environmental threshold for apparent binding/occupancy versus catalytic competence
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Different protonation-linked microstates can control chemistry at the catalytic step and substrate/inhibitor binding energetics with distinct environmental sensitivities, so the H-dependence of turnover need not align with the H-dependence of apparent binding/inhibition.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a second finite threshold inside the occupancy denominator, changing where H-curvature appears across substrate regimes rather than simply rescaling the whole response.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: One shared Hill-like environmental transition is sufficient for both catalytic competence and apparent affinity/substrate-inhibition behavior.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Catalytic competence and apparent binding/inhibition can have distinct environmental midpoints, with the denominator using K_H_app while the numerator competence term retains K_H.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: k_cat*E_total*S/(K_M*(1 + H/K_H) + S + S**2/K_I) + k_cat*E_total*S/(K_M*(1 + H/K_H) + S + S**2/K_I)*(1/(1 + (H/K_H)**n_H) - 1)
evolution_contract.after_fragment: k_cat*E_total*S/(K_M*(1 + H/K_H_app) + S + S**2/K_I) + k_cat*E_total*S/(K_M*(1 + H/K_H_app) + S + S**2/K_I)*(1/(1 + (H/K_H)**n_H) - 1)
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when K_H_app = K_H, so all H-dependence again shares one midpoint.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: When E_total, k_cat, and buffer composition aside from H are held fixed and H is swept across its transition region, low-S assays mainly follow the numerator competence transition, but assays at S near saturation or inhibition show shifted H-curvature because the denominator transition is governed by K_H_app. This changes the scored static mapping v0(S,H,...) itself, not merely an auxiliary quantity.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce substrate-dependent shifts in the apparent H midpoint because its denominator and numerator are locked to the same K_H. Retuning K_M, K_I, K_H, or n_H can move or sharpen one common transition, but cannot make low-S and high-S normalized v0(H) curves bend around different H scales within one shared model.

evolution_plan.promotion_reason: Existing symbols provide only one environmental scale K_H for all H effects. A distinct independently sampled condition is unnecessary, but one additional environmental-response input is needed if the benchmark requires separating the H sensitivity of binding/inhibition from that of catalytic competence without conflating them into the same shared transition.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes a single environmental threshold K_H controls every H-mediated effect, even though catalytic turnover and substrate-binding/inhibitory equilibria can shift with different protonation or conformational midpoints.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: One shared Hill-like environmental transition is sufficient for both catalytic competence and apparent affinity/substrate-inhibition behavior.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Different protonation-linked microstates can control chemistry at the catalytic step and substrate/inhibitor binding energetics with distinct environmental sensitivities, so the H-dependence of turnover need not align with the H-dependence of apparent binding/inhibition.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent response is effectively one H-threshold modulating the whole rate law: with enzyme amount fixed and assays taken as independent initial rates, varying H changes v0 through a single shared transition scale while varying S only moves the system along the same family of H-curves. A realistic next refinement is to relax that shared-threshold assumption. Hold E_total, k_cat, and other assay conditions fixed; vary H across below-to-above K_H and compare low-S assays with assays near saturation or substrate inhibition. In the parent, one refitted parameter set still predicts the same H midpoint structure across substrate regimes because all H-effects are tied to one K_H. In the child, the apparent H midpoint or curvature of v0 can differ between low and high S because denominator terms tied to binding/inhibitory occupancy respond to H differently from catalytic competence. This is scientifically admissible when H spans a range where protonation-linked changes are appreciable but enzyme integrity remains preserved. Limitation: if the sampled S range is narrowly confined to very low substrate, the contrast may be weak because affinity/inhibition contributions are then hard to observe.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

scenario_text: Measure the initial catalytic rate of a purified enzyme over a range of substrate concentrations while holding enzyme abundance and buffer conditions fixed. Reversible substrate capture creates a finite pool of occupied active sites, so the rate rises rapidly at low substrate and approaches a capacity limit at high substrate. Product accumulation is negligible during the measurement window, making each observation an independent instantaneous-rate experiment.
